flows.title: Home — Deals Queue & Navigation
flows.description: The portal opens on the queue, which is role-aware (2026-08-23): the Advisor gets a guided list (no filter pills, a Next line per deal), the Team Lead the original two-lane floor view (pills + archive). Both roles see the four identifiers on every row — name, VIN, stock, stage — with a chevron as the tap cue. There is no login: the app-bar role switch stands in for authentication, and the drawer holds global navigation and the demo reset.

screens.notes: The Advisor's guided view: no filter pills (the dashboard is the Team Lead's tool), the mono VIN + STK line under the name, the vehicle, and a 'Next: …' line in the stage colour from real deal state. A discovery deal would show no vehicle line at all until one is selected.

issues.issue: No authentication exists: the portal opens straight on the floor queue, with the Advisor / Team Lead switch standing in for identity.
issues.observation: By design for a demo/training tool — documented here so the absence of a login flow is not read as missing documentation.

flows.title: Scan Driver's License
flows.description: The prop-licence scanner as the Granola-discipline journey (owner's flow mockup + 34-section design prompt, 2026-08-25): a quiet dot header, serif headings, one soft document surface per group, read-mode-first reviews with editing in bottom sheets, and one dominant action per screen. Only the five printed training props can ever be recognised; anything else is refused with a teaching message. Prop 1 matches a seed customer by name (ambiguous → compare), prop 2 carries a licence on file (confident match), 3–5 create new customers. Phone AND email are both required on every customer record; the scan asks for no credit score.

screens.notes: The journey owns the phone screen. One quiet header row: a bare ← / ×, five step dots, and the gold TRAINING · PROPS ONLY chip — no wordmark, no boxed icons, no help control. Serif page heading, one supporting sentence, two benefit rows sitting on the page rather than in cards.

The camera is the one dark surface and owns the middle of the screen: corner brackets, flash bolt and shutter drawn as illustration, one instruction line. The phone's own camera opens on tap — there is no live viewfinder (invariant 5), so none of the three is its own control. Upload fallback beneath.
Barcode silhouette in the frame, and 'Front captured' with a Retake front control. This is the side the recognizer actually reads.

Whitespace, a modest green ring, and three rows that tick only as each step really finishes: reading licence, finding customer, verifying details. A stranded read cannot paint over a later screen — the run carries a generation token.

screens.action: Tap Retake photo / Enter license manually
screens.notes: Recovery, not punishment: what to fix, then the demo limit in a quiet line. No cause diagnosis — the recognizer finds a prop marker or refuses; there is no code path that reads a real ID.

screens.action: Type a licence number, tap Search
screens.notes: A CRM SEARCH by licence number and state — never a card read. Nothing typed here is treated as licence data recovered from the card, so its 'create' hands off to the full Create Customer form.
The found customer on one document surface with a quiet 'License match' pill. A miss says plainly that nothing in the records carries that number.

Shown for EVERY match now, not only ambiguous ones — the advisor sees who the scan resolved to before anything attaches. Trimmed to identity facts; no CRM metadata. The pill states the REAL basis (License match / Name and birthday match / Name match / Same birthday), never an invented confidence. When the match is only a guess the scanned licence is shown beneath, so the two can be compared.

Summary-first (decision 11, reversed by the owner) and read-mode-first: values render as text on one document surface, with a quiet gold 'Updated from license · was …' line on each field the licence changed, and 'n fields will be updated' by the pinned action.

Edit is a word, not a pill, and it opens a focused bottom sheet — handle, serif title, the granular inputs, one Save. Never a modal inside a modal; outside tap and Escape both close it. EVERY field in a sheet is required to save (owner, 2026-08-25); the one exception is the middle name, which a guest may not have.

screens.action: Type a phone already on file, tap Create Customer
screens.notes: The licence already filled these in, so they are read-first rows; the only typing asked for is what the licence cannot say. Contact is phone and email — both required, and no credit score is asked for at the door.

The page stays calm — crimson touches only the conflicting number itself. No licence carries a phone number, so this compares the number just TYPED against the record already holding it, and states what each action does.

screens.action: Read the code back, tap Verify & Link
screens.notes: Linking overwrites someone's existing record off a typed number, so it is gated (owner, 2026-08-25): a 6-digit code goes to that number and the guest reads it back. A wrong code marks the field and merges nothing. The demo has no network path, so the sheet says plainly that no text was really sent and shows the code the guest would have received.

flows.title: Client Document Upload (customer's phone)
flows.description: What the customer sees from the text link, rebuilt from the owner's upload prototype (2026-08-27) in Ride Price colours. This is the customer's OWN page: no app bar, no role switch, no debug strip — a white edge-to-edge canvas reached from a text message by someone who does not work at the dealership. One row per requested document with a line icon and a plain what-to-bring subtitle, an "n of N ready" progress line, and one dominant action. Verification is simulated with scripted beats (the licence needs both sides, insurance flags once, two paystubs). An unreadable photo is refused plainly — "Too blurry to read" — with the retake on the row, never a coaching screen.

screens.notes: The advisor sends the request; this is the message as the customer receives it. The link is the only way in — no account, no password.
The heading runs straight into the progress line — the explanatory paragraph was cut (owner, 2026-08-27): "0 of 3 ready" and the submit button already carry the send-when-ready model.
